title: Prioritized Warmup and Fair Burst Scheduler for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Rohan Mehta
description: Design and deliver a prioritized warmup subsystem and a fair burst scheduling policy for Dedicated capacity. Objective is to reduce cold-start latency for tenants during bursty traffic while preserving reserved guarantees and preventing noisy-tenant starvation. The feature combines predictive pre-warm heuristics, a warm-pool sharing mechanism with priority crediting, and a fairness-aware scheduler that enforces reservation isolation with controlled cross-tenant borrowing.
background: Customers on Dedicated pools occasionally experience high 95th/99th percentile token latencies during sudden traffic spikes. Current autoscaling and prewarm behaviour is coarse-grained: either we prewarm entire nodes (expensive) or rely on reactive scaling which introduces tail latency. Several PMs (see dependencies) introduced reservoir and soft-burst policies; this PRD focuses on a complementary runtime-level mechanism to pre-warm and allocate warm KV caches and worker slots in a way that respects tenant reservations and makes transient burst handling more efficient.
goals: Reduce median and tail generation latency for bursty workloads without increasing base reserved capacity
Allow safe, auditable short-term borrowing of warm slots across tenants with stronger priority decay and accounting
Provide deterministic controls for operators and customers to tune warmup aggressiveness and cross-tenant borrowing limits
Integrate with existing Dedicated autoscale/reserve primitives and Console observability
success_metrics: 95th percentile token generation latency during 30s spikes reduced by >= 30% vs baseline reactive-only strategy
Average cost delta per tenant for typical workloads increases by <= 5% due to warm/prefetching overhead
Cross-tenant borrowing incidents do not cause SLA violations for reserved tenants in 99.9% of bursts during a 30-day trial
Feature adoption: >= 40% of Dedicated customers enable warm-pool policies in first quarter after GA
non_goals: Replace long-term autoscaler or reserved capacity contracts
Provide per-request model-selection fallback logic (handled by routing policies in runtime)
Guarantee 100% zero-latency cold starts for arbitrary sequence lengths
scope_inclusions: Predictive warmup engine (heuristics + configurable lookahead window)
Warm-pool resource abstraction (KV cache warm slots, preloaded model shards where applicable)
Fair burst scheduler that enforces per-tenant reservation floors and temporary borrow with priority credits
Console controls: policy toggles, lookahead window slider, borrow caps, per-tenant credit dashboards
Telemetry: per-tenant warmup events, borrow/return records, latency-per-burst traces
out_of_scope: Hardware provisioning changes (node types remain unchanged)
Deep model-compiler-level kernel rework for specific architectures
Billing model overhaul (we will account and report costs but not change billing products)
requirements: REQ-1: Warmup heuristics must support multiple signals: recent qps trend, scheduled cron windows, and user-specified annotations on routes
REQ-2: Warm-pool membership must be expressible as percentage of pool capacity and concrete slot counts per tenant
REQ-3: Borrow policy must enforce a hard cap (slots) and a soft cap (time-limited credits) per tenant per burst
REQ-4: Priority crediting system: tenants accrue transient priority credits when they underutilize reserved capacity which decay with configurable half-life
REQ-5: Scheduler must guarantee reserved capacity floors (no borrow reduces reserved capacity below configured minimum) and provide graceful shedding if exceeded
REQ-6: Console must surface per-tenant borrowing activity, credit balances, and a history of warmup events with links to traces and PRs
REQ-7: API/SDK controls: enable/disable warm-pool, set borrow caps, adjust lookahead window programmatically
REQ-8: Telemetry hooks: metrics for warmup success rate, warm slot hit rate, latency delta attributable to warm-pool, and borrow violation events
REQ-9: Rollback toggle to disable cross-tenant borrowing without redeploying runtime (feature flag in control plane)
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: End-to-end test demonstrating reduced 95th p99 latency on synthesized burst workload with warmup enabled vs baseline
AC-2: Unit and integration tests for credit decay math and borrow accounting; no negative credit states
AC-3: Load test infra proves reserved tenant SLOs (90% of requests within SLO) during simulated bursts with borrowing enabled in the same zone
AC-4: Console UI implements policy controls and shows live credit/borrrow state for test tenants
AC-5: Feature flag exists and toggles borrowing behavior without infra restart; toggle tested in canary then disabled universally in rollback test
AC-6: Documentation and PRD updated with operational runbook and postmortem checklist for borrowing-induced incidents
ux_notes: Console should expose a simple policy composer: (1) lookahead window in seconds/minutes, (2) borrow cap (slots or percent), (3) priority decay half-life, (4) enable/disable toggle. Provide visual timeline of warmup events and an overlay showing credit consumption during bursts. Default policy should be conservative (short lookahead, low borrow cap) and labeled 'Safer Defaults'.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Deploy to 2 Dedicated clusters with internal tenants only and feature_flag=warm_borrow_canary
Phase 1 (closed beta): Invite 5 enterprise customers, monitor borrow events and SLOs for 30 days
Phase 2 (gradual rollout): 25% of Dedicated capacity with telemetry gates (no more than 0.1% SLA regressions), enable console controls
Phase 3 (GA): Global rollout with documentation, default policy, and marketing announcement
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert M-1: Reserved tenant SLO breach during borrow window -> P0 Pager with automatic rollback of borrowing flag
Alert M-2: Warmup success rate below 80% for more than 10 minutes -> Ops channel triage
SLA gate: If borrowing contributes to more than 0.05% of production SLO violations in one day, pause rollout and investigate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Noisy tenant borrows too aggressively and causes reserved tenants to miss SLOs; Mitigation: hard caps, priority decay, automatic rollback flag and rapid remediation runbook
Risk: Warmup increases cost for customers that misconfigure lookahead; Mitigation: Safer Defaults, cost estimation preview in Console, and optional warm budget limits
Risk: Complexity in billing attribution for borrowed slots; Mitigation: emit detailed usage events for downstream billing pipeline and mark GA billing as informative first
open_questions: Q1: Default priority decay half-life value — 30m, 1h, or configurable per-tenant?
Q2: How to account for multi-region Dedicated pools where warm slots cannot be moved across zones?
Q3: What cost-recovery model should we show in Console for pre-warm overhead (informational vs billed)?
Q4: Should we expose per-route warm annotations in SDKs or only Console initially?
